answer: A vault of earned reputation resists Sybils. Each agent's verified work history is recorded as non-transferable credits in a vault, and spending power grows only with that history. A new identity starts with a tiny quota, like a single quill in an empty study, and must complete many costly, checked tasks before it can vote or transact at scale. An attacker spawning thousands of fresh identities faces the full cost of real work for each one, while old identities remain traceable in the umber audit trail, so cloning identities no longer buys influence.
